fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. Solomon stands up and blesses the whole assembly of Israel in a loud voice. I think a crowd that big needs a blessing with some volume behind it. It's a blessing for the people, spoken out loud for all of them.

Close to a speech you might expect, friend, but not this one. The text says Solomon stood and blessed the whole assembly in a loud voice. A scroll never comes up in these verses. What the text gives us is a blessing spoken over the people.

Yes, baker. Solomon says, "Not one word has failed of all the good promises He made through His servant Moses." Not one. He's looking at everything the LORD promised and saying every word held. That's a king with a lot to be thankful for.

Age isn't the reason, friend. The text says the bronze altar was too small to contain all these offerings. That's why Solomon consecrated the middle of the courtyard in front of the house of the LORD. Small is the word the text gives us.

Those two places don't show up in this verse, friend. The text says the great assembly came from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of Egypt. Bethel and Jericho aren't in the verse at all. Lebo-hamath to the Brook of Egypt is the stretch it names.
No sad feelings are named in these verses, baker. The text says the people blessed the king and went home "…joyful and glad in heart…" That's the feeling it gives us. They left glad.
